Lutowiska Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lutowiska, Poland

Not demolished. Likely established in the second half of the 18th century on a hill roughly 400m from the village center, this cemetery served Lutowiska and several surrounding towns, including Polany, Skorodny, Stuposiany, and Zatwarnica. Unusually, it survived WWII in fairly good condition and saw no mass executions on-site - a rarity among Jewish cemeteries in the region, making it, alongside Lesko's, one of the best-preserved in south-eastern Poland, though it has never been entered into Poland's monument register. The area's Jews were instead murdered by Ukrainian forces on the night of June 22-23, 1942, near the local church.
